questions.question: Which of the following does NOT have an opportunity cost?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sunlight**__ does NOT have an opportunity cost.
 
• Opportunity cost is the loss of benefit or value that would have been derived from an option that is not chosen.
 
• In other words, it is the profit lost when one alternative is selected over another.
 
• For instance, when a farmer chooses to plant wheat; the opportunity cost is planting a different crop.
 
• In the given case, sunlight is classified as a free good. A free good is a resource that is so abundant that its availability is not a constraint on economic activity.
 
• Additionally, a free good is a good with zero opportunity cost.
 
• This means it can be consumed in as much quantity as needed without reducing its availability to others.
 
• Free goods like air, water and sunshine have zero opportunity cost because their total supply exceeds total demand.
 
• Therefore, no sacrifice has to be made to obtain them.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties made Kanauj (Kanyakubja) it's the capital city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pratihara dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pratihara dynasty**__

 __
 
• This dynasty made **Kanauj (Kanyakubja) **it's the capital city.
 
• They ruled during 8th-11th Century A.D.
 
• The Pratiharas were also renamed as Gurjara Pratiharas.
 
• The Gurjara Pratihara dynasty was founded by **Nagabhata I** in the Malwa region in the 8th century.
 
• Pratihara dynasty gained importance during the reign of Nagabhatta I, who ruled between 730- 756 C.E. He was successful against the Arabs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sena dynasty**

 
 
• The Sena Dynasty ruled from Bengal through the 11th and 12th centuries.
 
• During its peak, the Sena empire covered much of the northeastern region of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The dynasty was founded by Samanta Sena, who was part of the Pala Empire and usurped the power when the pala empire began to weaken.
 
• He was succeeded by Vijaya Sena who strengthened the foundations of the dynasty, in his long reign of over 60 years.
 
• His son Ballala Sena conquered the Gaur region from Pala and became the ruler of the Bengal Delta.
 
 
 
• **Chola dynasty**
 
 
• The dynasty emerged in the ​9th century AD (850-1279 AD).
 
• The founder of the Chola Dynasty - Vijayalaya Vijayalaya captured Tanjore in 850 AD.
 
• The greatest Chola ruler was Rajaraja (985-1014 AD) and Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD).
 
• Rajaraja built Brihadeshwara temple / Rajarajeshwara temple (attributed to Shiva) at Tanjore. 
 
• Rajendra I defeated the Pala king Mahipala and took the title of Gangaikondachola and built a city called Gangaikondacholapuram. King Rajasimha built the Kailashnath temple at Kancheepuram.
 
• The last ruler of the Chola dynasty was Rajendra III.
 
• The Chola empire was divided into Mandalas (Province) and these were divided into Valanadu (Comissionary), Nadu (District), and Kurram ( a group of villages).
 
 
 
• **Pala dynasty**
 
 
• Its founder, Gopala, was a local chieftain who rose to power in the mid-8th century during a period of anarchy.
 
• His successor, Dharmapala, greatly expanded the kingdom and for a while was in control of Kannauj.

questions.question: ______ is a draft of a legislative proposal before the House.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A bill**__ is a draft of a legislative proposal before the House. 
 
• All legislative proposals have to be brought in the form of Bills before Parliament.
 
• A Bill is a statute in the draft and cannot become law unless it has received the approval of both the Houses of Parliament and the assent of the President of India.
 
• The process of lawmaking begins with the introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament.
 
• A Bill can be introduced either by a Minister or a member other than a Minister.
 
• In the former case, it is called a Government Bill and in the latter case, it is known as a Private Member's Bill.
 
• A Bill undergoes three readings in each House, i.e., the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha before it is submitted to the President for assent.
 
• After a Bill has been finally passed by the Houses of Parliament, it is submitted to the President for his assent.
 
• After a Bill has received the assent of the President, it becomes the law of the land.

questions.question: In which part of the human body will you find the 'superior rectus'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eye**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The superior rectus is one of the extrinsic muscles of the **eye**__.
 
• It is located outside the eyeball but within the orbit.
 
• It has a primary action of elevating the eye, causing the cornea to move superiorly.
 
• It belongs to a group called the extraocular muscles. This group of muscles serves to move the eyes within the orbit.
 
• It includes-
 
 
• superior rectus 
 
• inferior rectus
 
• medial rectus
 
• lateral rectus
 
• superior oblique
 
• inferior oblique muscles
 
 
 
• The four recti muscles all arise from a connective tissue ring called the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zin).

questions.question: Which chemical reaction takes place during the cooking of meat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Maillard reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Maillard reaction**__

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned food its distinctive flavour.
 
• Like caramelization, it is a form of non-enzymatic browning.
 
• **It takes place during the cooking of meat**.
 
• The reactive carbonyl group of the sugar interacts with the nucleophilic amino group of the amino acid, and interesting but poorly characterized odour and flavour molecules result.
 
 
 
• ** The Gattermann reaction**
 
 
• It is a chemical reaction in which aromatic compounds are formulated by a mixture of hydrogen cyanide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst.
 
 
 
• **The Swartz reaction**
 
 
• It is a reaction in which alkyl fluoride are formed when alkyl bromide or chloride reacts with metal fluorides.
 
 
 
• **The Finkelstein reaction**
 
 
• It is a preparation of alkyl iodide from alkyl bromide or chloride with potassium or sodium iodide in acetone.
